properties.name: Lame-Burra Game Reserve
properties.vegetation: Northern Guinea savanna grading to Sudan savanna; riparian forest.
properties.fauna: Roan antelope, hartebeest, buffalo, red-flanked duiker, red-fronted gazelle, lion (very low/possibly extinct), 101 bird spp. incl. Abyssinian ground hornbill, bateleur
properties.tourism: Remote savanna wilderness; proposed for merger with Falgore GR and upgrade to national park.
properties.threats: Poaching, illegal grazing, chemical fishing, bush fires, illegal land allocations, banditry.
properties.notes: Large savanna reserve in north-west Bauchi; part of the Falgore and Lame Burra IBA/KBA; under heavy encroachment.

properties.name: Kuyambana Game Reserve
properties.fauna: Savanna mammals, elephants recorded in the Kamuku–Kwiambana complex (80 counted in 1993)
properties.tourism: Contiguous with Kamuku National Park to the south; wilderness potential but currently insecure.
properties.threats: Banditry and kidnapping hideouts, encroachment, poaching.
properties.notes: Lies north of Kamuku National Park (Kaduna). Widely reported as a bandit stronghold; access unsafe.

properties.name: Dagida Game Reserve
properties.authority: Niger State Ministry of Environment & Forest Resources
properties.notes: WDPA reports 294.2 km2; Niger State lists 'Dagina Games Reserve' in Lavun LGA. Placed at Lavun HQ (Kutigi). Listed in the World Database on Protected Areas as 'Dagida' with a reported area of 294.22 km2.

properties.name: Alawa National Park
properties.authority: National Park Service; National Park Service (handover from Niger State; 2024)
properties.tourism: Newly upgraded park; tourism infrastructure planned.
properties.threats: Banditry in surrounding area.
properties.notes: Game reserve (29,620 ha, 1992 World Bank list); approved 2020 for upgrade to national park, Niger State transition committee Nov 2024 - overlaps national-park layer. Point is GeoNames Alawa FR. Former Alawa Game Reserve; presidential order 2020/2022, NASS approval Mar 2023; state transition committee Nov 2024. Coordinates approx at Alawa (Shiroro/Rafi area, unverified).

properties.name: Opara Game Reserve
properties.flora: Anogeissus leiocarpus, Vitellaria paradoxa, Faidherbia (Acacia) albida
properties.threats: Herder encroachment and insecurity reported in the Opara forest (2019); illegal land allocations later revoked
properties.notes: Largest Oyo reserve (~73% of state reserve area); 219,953 ha mapped in 2023 study. Gazetted as a game reserve in the former Western State together with Upper Ogun (reported by Geerling in Environmental Conservation, 1974). FAO's national forest resources study lists Opara among existing game reserves at 110,000 ha, managed by the state forestry department's wildlife section.

properties.name: Edumanom National Park
properties.authority: National Park Service; Bayelsa State Ministry of Environment
properties.flora: Swamp forest trees, raffia palms
properties.fauna: Chimpanzee (among Nigeria's last Delta populations), Sclater's guenon, olive colobus, Niger Delta red colobus, manatee, three crocodile species, Chimpanzee (last in Niger Delta), crocodiles
properties.tourism: Proposed as a national park; key primate site. Proposed chimpanzee tour packages by boat.
properties.threats: Oil industry, logging, hunting via pipelines, oil palm expansion, Ogbia–Nembe road.
properties.notes: Former Edumanom (Edumenum) Forest Reserve, largely community-managed; upgraded to national park 2023. Proposed by Rivers State in 1970; managed in practice as community forest.

properties.name: Taylor Creek Forest Reserve (Biseni forests)
properties.vegetation: Seasonally flooded freshwater swamp forest with forest lakes.
properties.flora: Raphia palms, Symphonia globulifera, Ficus
properties.fauna: Red-bellied guenon, pygmy hippopotamus, yellow-backed duiker, 96 bird species
properties.threats: Logging via oil-access roads, unregulated hunting.
properties.notes: Biseni forests KBA (216 km2); Taylor Creek also listed as a game reserve. FAO area 22,566 ha.

properties.name: Baturiya Wetland Game Reserve
properties.authority: Jigawa State Government (proposed transfer to National Park Service)
properties.vegetation: Sudano-Sahelian floodplain wetland, ponds and seasonally flooded fadama.
properties.flora: Mitragyna inermis, doum palm (Hyphaene thebaica), Borassus, Anogeissus leiocarpus, Acacia nilotica, baobab
properties.fauna: Waterfowl (pelicans, yellow-billed stork, knob-billed duck, white-faced whistling duck, garganey, ~197, 000 counted Jan 2001), crocodiles, monitor lizards, monkeys
properties.resources: Fisheries, grazing, flood-recession farming, water, fuelwood
properties.tourism: Major bird-watching wetland in the Hadejia-Nguru floodplain; research and field-study use, tourism development planned.
properties.threats: Reduced flooding from upstream Tiga and Challawa dams, drought, siltation, invasive grasses, overgrazing, fuelwood cutting.
properties.notes: Ramsar site (2008) within Hadejia-Nguru wetlands; among 10 game reserves approved by House of Reps for upgrade to national park.

properties.name: Sambisa Game Reserve
properties.vegetation: Sudan savanna woodland and dense thorn bush.
properties.flora: Acacia spp, baobab, tamarind, Terminalia, Diospyros mespiliformis, Balanites, Combretum
properties.fauna: Formerly elephant, roan antelope, leopard, spotted hyena, patas monkey, 62 bird spp. incl. Arabian bustard, once ostrich
properties.tourism: Former safari destination (lodges from 1970s), now inaccessible.
properties.threats: Insurgent (Boko Haram/ISWAP) occupation since 2013, landmines, poaching, fuelwood.
properties.notes: Colonial-era reserve; area 51,800 ha (FAO) vs 518 km2 (Wikipedia). Management abandoned since 2013.

properties.name: Kainji Lake National Park
properties.governance: Federal or national ministry or agency
properties.vegetation: Sudan-Guinea savanna woodland on hills and ironstone pans. Guinea forest-savanna mosaic on eroded sandstone plateau.
properties.flora: Burkea africana, Terminalia avicennioides, Detarium microcarpum, Isoberlinia tomentosa/doka, Diospyros mespiliformis, Afzelia africana, Daniellia oliveri, Pterocarpus erinaceus, Parkia, Vitellaria paradoxa, Khaya senegalensis, Uapaca togoensis
properties.fauna: Lion, leopard, elephant, hippo (Oli River), kob, roan, hartebeest, buffalo, ~350 birds, Nile crocodile, Savanna antelopes, monkeys (depleted by poaching)
properties.resources: Fisheries (Kainji Lake, 82 fish spp.), grazing, NTFPs
properties.tourism: Only sector developed for tourism: game drives, Oli River hippo pool, lodge at New Bussa HQ. No access roads; not developed for tourism.
properties.threats: Insecurity/banditry (operations suspended 2021), poaching, grazing. Overgrazing, erosion, heavy poaching.
properties.notes: Former Zugurma Game Reserve, SE of Kainji Lake. Coordinates at Zugurma village (approx). West of Kainji Lake; former Borgu Game Reserve. Coordinates at New Bussa HQ.
properties.other_names: Kainji Lake National Park – Zugurma Sector.

properties.name: Udi-Nsukka Game Reserve
properties.notes: Listed by FAO (1990s) as a 5,600 ha game reserve/wildlife sanctuary; exact location and current status unclear. Placed approx at Udi. Listed by FAO as an existing game reserve of 5,600 ha (WDPA reported area 56 km2), managed by the state forestry department's wildlife section.

properties.name: Ologbo Forest Reserve
properties.vegetation: Freshwater swamp forest with rainforest and fallow land
properties.flora: Lovoa trichilioides, Entandrophragma sp., Millettia sp., Cleistopholis patens, Ficus spp., Musanga cecropioides
properties.threats: Degradation of floristic value; conversion to fallow land
properties.notes: FAO lists Ologbo forest reserve at 17,784 ha (freshwater swamp) and Ologbo game reserve at 19,440 ha (WDPA: 194.4 km2). A 2015 survey of the Ologbo concession recorded 71 woody species in 27 families; rainforest and swamp plots were more diverse than fallow.

properties.name: Okomu National Park
properties.flora: Ceiba pentandra (kapok), Triplochiton scleroxylon, Antiaris africana, Alstonia congensis, 60 medicinal spp
properties.fauna: Forest elephant, white-throated guenon (endemic), sitatunga, red river hog, Maxwell's duiker, dwarf crocodile, ~150 birds, 700+ butterflies
properties.tourism: Forest trails, two tree houses (one 43 m up a silk-cotton tree), chalets, guided walks and birding.
properties.threats: Illegal logging, poaching, farm encroachment, oil-palm/rubber plantations around park.
properties.notes: Wildlife sanctuary 1935 within Okomu Forest Reserve; national park 1999.

properties.name: Cross River National Park
properties.governance: Federal or national ministry or agency
properties.designations: IBA; KBA; UNESCO MAB (Oban); UNESCO MAB (Okwangwo)
properties.vegetation: Lowland and submontane rainforest, montane grassland on ridges. Lowland Guineo-Congolian rainforest (Pleistocene refuge).
properties.flora: ~1, 568 plant spp. (77 endemic to Nigeria): African mahogany, red ironwood (Lophira alata), African corkwood, epiphytic ferns and orchids, 545 spp. in 98 families incl. Ancistrocladus korupensis, Prunus africana, ebony
properties.fauna: Forest elephant, chimpanzee, drill, Sclater's guenon, 75+ mammals, 350+ birds (incl. olive ibis), 42 snakes, ~950 butterflies, Cross River gorilla, Nigeria-Cameroon chimpanzee, Preuss's guenon, grey-necked rockfowl, golden greenbul, grey parrot
properties.resources: Timber, bushmeat, NTFPs (bush mango, Afang/Gnetum), watershed, NTFPs, medicinal plants
properties.tourism: Kanyang tourist village ~1 h from Calabar, Kwa Falls, Agbokim Falls, forest hiking and birding; contiguous with Korup NP (Cameroon). Gorilla tracking, hiking near the Obudu Plateau; borders Takamanda NP (Cameroon).
properties.threats: Illegal logging, slash-and-burn farming, hunting, chemical fishing, plantations at margins. Logging, snaring/poaching, farming, cattle grazing.
properties.notes: Formed from Boshi, Okwangwo and Boshi Extension Forest Reserves; Cross River gorilla stronghold. Southern and larger division of CRNP, carved from Oban Group Forest Reserve.
properties.other_names: Cross River National Park – Okwangwo Division.

properties.name: Yankari Game Reserve
properties.vegetation: Sudan-Guinea savanna with riparian forest along Gaji river.
properties.flora: Savanna woodland, riparian forest, wild baobab, Borassus palms, Isoberlinia doka, Daniellia oliveri, Anogeissus leiocarpa, Vitellaria paradoxa
properties.fauna: Savanna elephant, lion (near extinct), hippo, buffalo, roan, waterbuck, baboons, 350+ birds (saddle-billed stork), African bush elephant, lion, roan antelope, hartebeest, baboon, 350+ bird spp
properties.resources: Warm springs, NTFPs, Water (Gaji, Yashi, Yuli streams), wildlife
properties.tourism: Nigeria's best-known wildlife destination: Wikki Warm Springs, game drives, Marshall Caves, Dukke iron-smelting furnaces.
properties.threats: Poaching, grazing incursions; lion near extinction. Poaching (elephant), grazing, decline of lions.
properties.notes: Constituted as Bauchi NA forest reserve 1957, opened as game reserve 1962; national park 1991-2006, then returned to state as game reserve.
properties.other_names: Yankari Game Reserve (former Yankari National Park).

properties.name: Old Oyo National Park
properties.governance: Federal or national ministry or agency
properties.vegetation: Guinea savanna woodland with gallery forest and inselbergs.
properties.flora: Savanna woodland trees (Isoberlinia, Daniellia, Vitellaria), riparian forest
properties.fauna: Buffalo, kob, roan, western hartebeest, waterbuck, bushbuck, patas monkey, birds
properties.resources: Water (River Ogun, Ikere Gorge Dam), grazing, minerals
properties.tourism: Ruins of Oyo-Ile (old Oyo Empire capital), Ikere Gorge Dam, caves, rock shelters, inselberg climbing.
properties.threats: Poaching, logging, herder encroachment, illegal mining.
properties.notes: Formed from Upper Ogun (1936) and Oyo-Ile (1941) Forest Reserves.

properties.name: Gashaka-Gumti National Park
properties.governance: Federal or national ministry or agency
properties.vegetation: Guinea savanna (Gumti) to montane forest and grassland (Gashaka).
properties.flora: Afzelia africana, Khaya senegalensis, Daniellia oliveri, Isoberlinia doka, Vitellaria paradoxa, Triplochiton scleroxylon, Pterocarpus erinaceus
properties.fauna: Largest chimpanzee population in Nigeria, buffalo, elephant, giant eland, roan, leopard, lion (rare), wild dog, 500+ birds
properties.tourism: Chappal Waddi (2,419 m, Nigeria's highest peak), Kiri waterfall, hippo pool, hot spring, German fort ruins on Gashaka Hill.
properties.threats: Rosewood logging, grazing, poaching, insecurity.
properties.notes: Nigeria's largest national park; home to Gashaka Primate Project.

properties.name: Kamuku National Park
properties.governance: Federal or national ministry or agency
properties.vegetation: Sudan-Guinea savanna woodland with riparian forest.
properties.flora: Isoberlinia doka, Afzelia africana, Daniellia oliveri, Detarium, Terminalia avicennioides, Raphia, Andropogon gayanus
properties.fauna: Elephant, roan, western hartebeest, oribi, red-flanked duiker, patas monkey, baboon, 177 birds (secretarybird, ground hornbill, Denham's bustard)
properties.tourism: Elephants, Dogon Ruwa waterfalls, Goron Dutse inselberg, Tsaunin Rema boulder hill, birding.
properties.threats: Banditry (operations suspended 2021), hunting, cattle grazing.
properties.notes: Gazetted 1936 as Birnin Gwari Native Authority Forest Reserve; upgraded 1999.

properties.name: Yankari Forest Reserve
properties.vegetation: West African savanna; bush savanna on sandy soils east of the Gaji valley
properties.fauna: African bush elephant, olive baboon, patas monkey, roan antelope, lion, African buffalo, waterbuck, bushbuck, hippopotamus; 350+ bird species incl. saddle-billed stork, helmeted guineafowl, African grey hornbill
properties.tourism: Yankari is Nigeria's best-known wildlife destination, with several natural warm-water springs, and was opened to the public on 1 December 1962. Archaeological sites, including old iron-smelting furnaces and caves at Delimiri and Ampara, support heritage tourism.
properties.threats: Lion population reported to be close to local extinction; illegal activities
properties.notes: The game preservation area was approved in 1956, constituted as a Bauchi Native Authority Forest Reserve in 1957 and declared a national park by Decree 36 of 1991. National park status was withdrawn in 2006 at the Bauchi State Government's request. Wikipedia gives the area as about 2,244 km², compared with the atlas polygon's 2,134 km².

properties.name: Baturiya Wetland
properties.vegetation: Intermittent floodplain lakes and Acacia–doum palm woodland.
properties.flora: Acacia nilotica, Mitragyna inermis, doum palm, Borassus, baobab, wild rice
properties.fauna: Pelicans, yellow-billed stork, knob-billed duck, garganey, crocodiles, monitor lizards
properties.tourism: Birdwatching; part of Hadejia Wetlands NP.
properties.threats: Upstream dams, siltation, invasive grasses, illegal grazing.
properties.notes: Ramsar no. 1752; part of Hadejia-Nguru wetlands.

properties.name: Dagona Sanctuary Lake Ramsar Site
properties.governance: Federal or national ministry or agency
properties.designations: Chad Basin NP; IBA (Hadejia-Nguru wetlands); Ramsar; Waterfowl Sanctuary
properties.vegetation: Seasonally flooded oxbow lake in Hadejia-Jama'are floodplain. Seasonal oxbow lake with Mitragyna and doum palm woodland.
properties.flora: Mitragyna inermis, doum palm, Borassus, Acacia, Parkia, Khaya senegalensis
properties.fauna: 20, 000+ waterbirds: herons incl. goliath, egrets, pelicans, spur-winged goose, spoonbill, red-fronted gazelle, 25+ waterbird spp, wintering Palaearctic ducks, breeding grey heron, little egret, fishes
properties.tourism: Dagona Waterfowl Sanctuary: birdwatching base for the Hadejia-Nguru wetlands. Bird hides, platforms and nature trails in the Dagona Waterfowl Sanctuary.
properties.threats: Grazing and wild-resource collection despite prohibitions. Grazing, fuelwood, upstream dams, drought.
properties.notes: Dagona Waterfowl Sanctuary, Ramsar No. 1753; managed within the Bade-Nguru sector of Chad Basin NP.

properties.name: Upper Orashi Forests Ramsar Site
properties.flora: Lophira alata, Hallea ledermannii (abura), Sacoglottis, Ricinodendron, Irvingia, Raphia hookeri, rattan, Ricinodendron heudelotii, Albizia adianthifolia, Hallea ledermannii, oil palm
properties.fauna: Sclater's and white-throated guenons, Delta red colobus, pygmy hippo, black-fronted duiker, grey parrot roost, Sclater's guenon, white-throated guenon, red colobus
properties.tourism: Limited; research/education potential. Ecotourism limited by insecurity.
properties.threats: Uncontrolled logging, oil access roads, farm clearing, insecurity. Poaching, uncontrolled logging, militancy.
properties.notes: Ramsar site since 30 Apr 2008 (25,165 ha); forest reserve ~10,384 ha (FAO). Ramsar no. 1759; gazetted FR 9,696 ha within site.

properties.name: Foge Islands Ramsar Site
properties.vegetation: Seasonally flooded grassland islands in Kainji Lake.
properties.flora: Nymphaea lotus, Echinochloa, Vossia cuspidata, Cyperus, Andropogon, Hyparrhenia, Echinochloa pyramidalis, E. stagnina, Cyperus procerus
properties.fauna: 180+ birds (whistling ducks, pratincoles, spur-winged goose, glossy ibis), hippo, kob, waterbuck, hartebeest, 180+ bird spp. (white-faced whistling-duck, collared pratincole, blue-cheeked bee-eater)
properties.resources: Fishing (~5, 000 residents), recession farming, grazing, Fisheries
properties.tourism: Birding by boat on Lake Kainji next to Kainji Lake National Park.
properties.threats: Low lake levels and drought, overfishing, fuelwood cutting, hunting.
properties.notes: Island in Lake Kainji; permanently exposed parts lie in Kebbi State, western section in Niger State. Ramsar no. 1754; in northern Kainji Lake.

properties.name: Lake Chad Wetlands in Nigeria Ramsar Site
properties.vegetation: Lake, floodplain marsh, Typha/papyrus swamps and Sahel shrubland. Grasses, sedges, floating macrophytes, shrubs.
properties.flora: Typha australis, Cyperus papyrus, Mimosa pigra, Acacia nilotica, doum palm, Prosopis juliflora, wild rice
properties.fauna: 300+ birds (ferruginous duck, pallid harrier, great snipe), lungfish, Clarias, tilapia, Kouri cattle, Palaearctic waterbirds incl. marbled teal, indigenous fishes
properties.resources: Fishing, rice and recession farming, grazing, Fisheries, recession farming
properties.tourism: Limited by insecurity.
properties.threats: Lake recession, dams, desertification, overgrazing, Boko Haram insecurity. Lake recession from drought and upstream dams; insecurity.
properties.notes: Ramsar No. 1749; only traditional (Kanuri) management of fishing and farming rights. Largest Nigerian Ramsar site; unprotected.

properties.name: Apoi Creek Forests Ramsar Site
properties.vegetation: Tidal freshwater swamp forest, mangrove, marsh.
properties.flora: ~240 spp.: Rhizophora, Uapaca paludosa, Nauclea, Raphia, Irvingia, Hallea ledermannii, Pterocarpus soyauxii
properties.fauna: Niger Delta red colobus, dwarf crocodile, sitatunga, leopard, grey parrot, Hartlaub's duck, African skimmer, Niger Delta red colobus (endemic, CR), fish spawning grounds
properties.resources: Fishing, logging, salt, NTFPs, canoe carving, Fish, timber
properties.tourism: Community conservation areas around Apoi, Kokologbene and Gbanraun. Creek and boat tourism potential.
properties.threats: Logging canals, oil spills and flaring, hunting. Timber extraction via dug canals, hunting.
properties.notes: Ramsar site (30 Apr 2008); includes Apoi Creek FR (7,080 ha, FAO). Ramsar no. 1751; now within Apoi National Park.

properties.name: Lower Kaduna–Middle Niger Floodplain
properties.vegetation: Floodplain marsh, Mitragyna swamp forest, Guinea savanna.
properties.flora: Nymphaea lotus, Echinochloa, Vossia, Phragmites karka, Mitragyna, Mimosa pigra
properties.fauna: Rosy bee-eater and carmine bee-eater colonies, Hartlaub's duck, woolly-necked stork, grey pratincole, Gymnarchus, Lates, Heterotis fish
properties.resources: Fishing, fadama rice/sugarcane farming, grazing, fuelwood
properties.tourism: Bee-eater colonies and river birding.
properties.threats: Upstream dams (Kainji, Jebba, Shiroro), intensive fadama farming, overfishing.
properties.notes: Ramsar no. 1755; otherwise unprotected.

properties.name: Oguta Lake
properties.governance: Federal or national ministry or agency
properties.vegetation: Natural freshwater lake with swamp and relict forest.
properties.flora: Nymphaea lotus, Pistia, Vossia, Lophira alata, Pycnanthus, Ricinodendron, oil palm
properties.fauna: ~40 fish spp. (Chrysichthys, Lates, Tilapia), Sclater's guenon in relict forests
properties.resources: Fishing, transport, sand dredging, water supply
properties.tourism: Lakeside hotel and golf course, boat rides; Imo's largest natural lake.
properties.threats: Overfishing, dredging, sewage, algal blooms, gully erosion.
properties.notes: Ramsar no. 1757.

properties.name: Pandam and Wase Lakes
properties.vegetation: Savanna lakes with gallery forest and woodland.
properties.flora: Afzelia africana, Ceiba pentandra, Raphia sudanica, Isoberlinia doka, Parkia biglobosa, Vitellaria paradoxa
properties.fauna: West African manatee, hippo, Nile crocodile, roan, buffalo, 217 birds (Pel's fishing owl, long-toed lapwing)
properties.tourism: Annual fishing festival, birdwatching, Pandam tourist village (20 chalets).
properties.threats: Poaching, overfishing, grazing/burning, farm conversion.
properties.notes: Ramsar no. 1758.

properties.name: Chad Basin National Park – Chingurmi-Duguma Sector
properties.vegetation: Sudan–Guinea savanna to Sahel; Acacia–Balanites woodland
properties.flora: Acacia spp., Balanites aegyptiaca, elephant grass, wild sorghum
properties.fauna: Savanna elephant (~100 in 2007), black crowned crane, demoiselle crane, white stork, helmeted guineafowl
properties.tourism: Game viewing and birding near the Cameroon border; lodges abandoned, off-road access and camping needed.
properties.threats: Poaching, farming/grazing encroachment, Boko Haram insecurity
properties.notes: Largest of Chad Basin NP's three separate sectors; transboundary elephant range with Waza (Cameroon).

properties.name: Chad Basin National Park – Bade-Nguru Wetlands Sector
properties.vegetation: Seasonal floodplain wetlands, doum palm and Acacia woodland; includes 5 forest reserves
properties.flora: Hyphaene thebaica, Acacia spp., Mitragyna inermis, wild rice
properties.fauna: Palearctic migratory waterfowl (garganey, ruff), herons, pelicans, red-fronted gazelle
properties.tourism: Includes the Dagona Waterfowl Sanctuary with bird hides and trails; prime winter birdwatching.
properties.threats: Reduced flooding from upstream dams, quelea poisoning, cultivation, tree loss
properties.notes: Part of the Hadejia-Nguru wetlands complex.

properties.name: Chad Basin National Park – Bulatura Oases Sector
properties.vegetation: Swampy inter-dune valleys (oases) between Sahelian sand dunes
properties.flora: Doum palm, Acacia, Sahelian grasses
properties.fauna: Sahelian birds and small mammals (poorly documented)
properties.tourism: Scenic dune and oasis landscapes near the Niger border.
properties.threats: Desertification, grazing
properties.notes: Smallest sector of Chad Basin NP.

properties.name: Apoi National Park
properties.flora: Rhizophora mangroves, Raphia, Irvingia, Uapaca, Nauclea, Hallea ledermannii, Xylopia staudtii
properties.fauna: Niger Delta red colobus, Sclater's guenon (?), dwarf and Nile crocodile, sitatunga, leopard, grey parrot, Hartlaub's duck
properties.tourism: Riverine boat-based ecotourism potential.
properties.threats: Logging canals, oil spills, gas flaring, hunting, land-tenure disputes
properties.notes: Former Apoi Creek Forest Reserve (Ramsar 2008); upgraded to national park (NASS approval 2023). Area is Ramsar boundary.

properties.name: Hadejia Wetlands National Park
properties.vegetation: Seasonal floodplain wetlands with Acacia–doum palm woodland
properties.flora: Acacia nilotica, Mitragyna inermis, Hyphaene thebaica, Borassus, Anogeissus leiocarpus, baobab, wild rice
properties.fauna: Pelicans, yellow-billed stork, knob-billed duck, white-faced whistling duck, garganey (20,000+ waterbirds), crocodiles
properties.tourism: Waterbird watching in the dry season; state tourism development planned.
properties.threats: Upstream dams (Tiga, Challawa), siltation, invasive Typha, illegal grazing/fuelwood
properties.notes: Former Baturiya Wetland Game Reserve; FG took over 10 Sep 2024. Area is Ramsar boundary.

properties.name: Kampe National Park
properties.authority: National Park Service (handover from Kwara State, 2025).
properties.tourism: Planned ecotourism; named after the Kampe River.
properties.notes: WDPA lists Ebbe/Kampe at 117.3 km2; approved in 2020 for upgrade to national park and handed to the Federal Government in Feb 2025 (overlaps national-park layer). Coordinates are GeoNames River Kampe FR. Former Kampe (Ebbe/Kampe) forest and game reserve; handed to NPS Feb 2025. LGA as reported by ThisDay; coordinates approx.

properties.name: Marhai National Park
properties.vegetation: Guinea savanna with gallery forest on escarpment. Guinea savanna and hills.
properties.fauna: Diverse wildlife (undocumented), Monkeys, guinea fowl
properties.tourism: Contains Farin Ruwa waterfall (~150 m), picnic site, Kulere culture. Scenic landscape; ecotourism, research and education planned. Promoted by the state for eco-tourism, research and education for its scenic landscape and wildlife.
properties.notes: Gazetted 1960 by Northern Region; upgraded to national park (FG takeover Dec 2024) - overlaps national-park layer. Former Marhai (Marhi) Forest Reserve; upgrade process began 2011; FG takeover Dec 2024. In Wamba LGA; the upgrade effort began in 2011 and in December 2024 the Federal Government took over management for the National Park Service as a national park.

properties.name: Pandam National Park
properties.authority: Plateau State Government (approved 2020 for NP upgrade). National Park Service.
properties.vegetation: Sudan-Guinea savanna with gallery forest; Pandam Lake (~2 km²).
properties.flora: Afzelia africana, Ceiba pentandra, Raphia sudanica, Burkea africana, Isoberlinia doka
properties.fauna: West African manatee, hippo, roan, buffalo, duikers, warthog, 217 birds (Pel's/Bouvier's fishing owl, long-toed lapwing), hippopotamus, roan antelope, buffalo (formerly), olive baboon, white-faced whistling duck, Pel's fishing owl
properties.tourism: Game viewing, birding, sport fishing, canoeing on Pandam Lake; 20 chalets (dilapidated). Pandam Lake boating, sport fishing, bird watching, chalets (some derelict).
properties.threats: Poaching, grazing, bush burning, logging, illegal fishing, encroachment. Poaching, grazing, bush burning, neglect, floodplain rice schemes.
properties.notes: Game reserve since 1972; one of 10 reserves approved in 2020 for upgrade to national park - may overlap national-park layer. Pandam Wildlife Park/Game Reserve (1972); upgraded to national park (NASS approval 2023). KBA gives 33,048 ha.

properties.name: Nguru Lake (and Marma Channel) Complex
properties.vegetation: Floodplain lakes, channels and marshes with doum palm uplands. Sahelian floodplain lake, marsh and fadama.
properties.flora: Echinochloa, Nymphaea, Typha, Ceratophyllum, doum palm, tamarind, wild rice
properties.fauna: Garganey (20, 000+ wintering), ruff, white-faced whistling duck, ~65 fish spp, white-faced whistling duck (each >20, 000), disc tilapia
properties.resources: Fisheries, recession farming, grazing, fuelwood, groundwater recharge, flood-recession farming
properties.tourism: Boat rides and birdwatching; IUCN wetland information centre. Boat-based ecotourism at Dabar Magini; winter birdwatching.
properties.threats: Typha invasion, upstream dams, grazing, cultivation, overfishing. Invasive Typha, upstream dams, overgrazing, fuelwood harvest.

properties.notes: Floodplain of Hadejia and Jama'are rivers; contains Baturiya Wetland GR (Jigawa) and several forest reserves; c. 35% under protection.
